title: Vacuuming: inspect, clear, control the cord and shut down safely
audience: Cleaners who use plug-in vacuums on hard floors, carpets, upholstery and stairs.
learningOutcomes: Pick up large and sharp objects by hand before vacuuming, using gloves for sharp items.
Vacuum systematically, with extra passes over heavy-traffic areas, edges and corners.
Control the cord so that it stays behind the operator and is never overstretched.
Shut down the machine, wind the cord and store the machine in its allocated place.

instruction.heading: Check the machine before the first pass
instruction.body: A vacuum is only as safe as its condition. Before you start, check the cord, plug, hose, wheels, filter and bag or container against the business's inspection checklist. If the machine fails any check, do not use it. Set it aside and report it, as “Site rules: approved products, plug-in equipment and reporting” describes. Also confirm the machine suits the job. A vacuum rated for dry dust may not be suitable for wet debris or unknown material, and “Vacuum systems” sets out how to match the machine to the job.

instruction.heading: Clear large and sharp objects first
instruction.body: Before you switch the machine on, pick up large objects by hand. These include bottle caps, coins, nails, pieces of packaging and any debris that could block the hose, jam the brush roll or strike you. Pick up sharp objects such as glass fragments with protective gloves, and place them in the sharps container or the waste container the business specifies. Vacuuming over glass or metal can damage the machine and injure the operator or other people in the room.

instruction.heading: Sequence and passes
instruction.body: Vacuum the area in a systematic pattern rather than wandering across it. Give extra attention to heavy-traffic routes, along skirting boards and in corners, where soil collects. Overlap each pass slightly so that no strip is missed. Plan the route so that you do not step on the cord or drag the machine across it.

instruction.heading: Controlling the cord
instruction.body: Keep the cord behind you as you move, so that it is never under the machine's wheels or in front of your feet. Do not overstretch the cord, because a tight cord can pull the plug or damage the cord where it meets the machine. Do not pull the machine by its cord, and do not run it over the cord. Keep cords out of doorways and off stairs, and follow “Stairs, balustrades and handrails: stable stance and safe layout” when you vacuum stairs or landings.

instruction.heading: Shutting down, winding and storing
instruction.body: When you finish, switch off the power at the machine before you unplug it. Then switch off the socket and remove the plug at the plug body, as “Site rules: approved products, plug-in equipment and reporting” describes. Wind the cord back onto the machine in a controlled way, keeping it off the floor and away from the wheels. Empty or service the bag or container as the procedure directs, then store the machine in its allocated place. A machine left in a walkway is a trip hazard, and others may use it or damage it.

procedure: Inspect the cord, plug, hose, filter and container against the business checklist before the first pass.
Pick up large and sharp objects by hand, using gloves for sharp items, and place them in the specified container.
Vacuum systematically, with extra passes over heavy-traffic areas, edges and corners.
Keep the cord behind you, not overstretched and not under the wheels.
Switch off the machine, then the socket, then remove the plug at the plug body. Wind the cord back in a controlled way.
Empty or service the container as directed, and store the machine in its allocated place.

workedExamples.situation: In a hallway the vacuum suddenly stops. You find a piece of glass has jammed the brush roll.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do before you restart?
workedExamples.reasoning: Switch off the machine at the machine, switch off the socket, and remove the plug at the plug body before you touch the brush roll. Remove the glass with gloves using the sharps method in the procedure. Check the brush roll for damage and look for other fragments before you continue. Report the glass to the supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: You are vacuuming a carpeted stair runner. The cord lies across the next step, and you lean back over the stairs to reach the far edge.
workedExamples.reasoning: Move the cord clear of the stairs so that you are not stepping on it, and do not lean out over the stairs to reach an edge. Keep your feet on the stair and move your position instead. Follow “Stairs, balustrades and handrails: stable stance and safe layout” for the stair and landing rules.

workedExamples.situation: You finish a carpeted office and leave the machine in the corridor, with the cord still lying on the floor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the correct end of the task?
workedExamples.reasoning: Switch off at the machine, switch off the socket, remove the plug at the plug body, wind the cord, and move the machine to its allocated storage place. A machine and loose cord in a corridor are a trip hazard for other people.

equipmentAndPpe: Vacuum with a current start-of-job inspection record
Sharps container or the waste container the business specifies
Warning sign for wet or occupied areas, where the procedure requires one

commonErrors.error: Starting the machine before large or sharp objects have been cleared.
commonErrors.prevention: Pick up large and sharp items by hand first, using gloves for sharp items.

commonErrors.error: Letting the cord run under the machine or across a doorway.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the cord behind you and out of walkways, and plan each pass around it.

commonErrors.error: Pulling the plug by the cord, or unplugging before switching off.
commonErrors.prevention: Switch off the machine and the socket, then remove the plug at the plug body.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the machine in a walkway at the end of the task.
commonErrors.prevention: Wind the cord and store the machine in its allocated place.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The business's testing and inspection regime applies.
Sharp and glass waste is handled under the business's sharps procedure.
Vacuuming dust or unknown material is covered in “Vacuum systems” and is not changed by this lesson.

qualityStandard: The machine passes the inspection check before its first use.
Large and sharp objects are removed by hand before the machine runs.
The full area is covered in a systematic pattern, with no cord under the machine.
The machine is switched off at the machine and at the socket, the cord is wound, and the machine is stored in its allocated place.
documentationEvidence: Equipment inspection record for the day, showing the machine passed the check.
Incident or hazard record for any glass, sharp object or equipment fault.
summary: Inspect the machine, then clear large and sharp objects by hand.
Vacuum systematically, with extra passes where soil collects.
Control the cord. Never pull the machine by it, and do not let it trip anyone.
Switch off the machine and the socket, unplug at the plug body, wind the cord and store the machine.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before you start vacuuming a room, what should you do first?
options: Start the machine on its lowest setting to test the brush roll
Pick up large and sharp objects by hand, using gloves for sharp items
Vacuum the edges last so that they stay clean and the floor stays tidy

knowledgeChecks.question: How should the cord be managed while you vacuum?
options: Kept behind you and not overstretched
Pulled ahead of you so that you can see it
Run under the machine to keep it out of the way

knowledgeChecks.question: You have finished and want to store the vacuum. What is the correct order?
options: Remove the plug by pulling the cord, then switch off the machine and wind the cord loosely
Leave the plug in the socket and wind the cord back and store the machine by the door for the next shift
Switch off the machine and the socket, remove the plug at the plug body, wind the cord, then store it
